title: Systems and methods for magnetic gripping

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
features.note: The abstract describes a magnetic gripping system (housing) with tunable gripping states (displaceable magnet) and implies interaction with an object (workpiece contact surfaces).
features.refuted: Quote only mentions tunable gripping states with different magnetic field strengths, does not teach housing, displaceable magnet, or pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: moving one or more of said first arrangement of magnets and said second arrangement of magnets to vary their position relative to one another to vary said first magnetic interaction, said second magnetic interaction, or both, to vary said magnetic
features.note: The reference explicitly states that magnets are moved relative to one another to vary magnetic flux, which corresponds to displacing a magnet between gripping and release positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: a plurality of pole members, wherein said plurality of pole members is at least partially disposed through said gripping surface.
features.note: The 'plurality of pole members' are analogous to pole shoes, and the 'gripping surface' acts as the workpiece contact surface, with the pole members disposed through it.
features.refuted: Quote mentions pole members disposed through gripping surface but does not teach attachment to housing or workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: each pole member of said plurality of pole members is configured to transfer magnetic flux caused by said first magnetic interaction and said second magnetic interaction to said object
features.note: The pole members are explicitly configured to transfer magnetic flux to the object, which is equivalent to guiding the magnetic field to the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not disclose any specific angles or orientations of the workpiece contact surface relative to the magnet displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: While the reference discloses a magnetic gripper with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes, it does not specify the contact surface angle relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
features.note: The abstract describes a magnetic gripping system for gripping an object, implying that in a gripping state, the magnetic force holds the object against contact surfaces.
features.refuted: Quote only mentions tunable gripping states with different magnetic field strengths, does not teach magnet in gripping position pressing workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: The reference does not describe the orientation of the housing or the displacement direction relative to any longitudinal axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: each pole member of said plurality of pole members is configured to transfer magnetic flux caused by said first magnetic interaction and said second magnetic interaction to said object
features.note: The pole members are configured to transfer magnetic flux, which implies they have a structure for directing the magnetic field portion to the object.
features.refuted: Quote teaches pole members transfer magnetic flux but does not teach an active structure for directing the magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles of an active structure on the pole members.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference mentions 'plurality of pole members' but does not describe them as having multiple projections or specific active structures for forming the contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections, recesses, or their dimensional relationships.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any positioning devices for the workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: each pole member of said plurality of pole members is configured to transfer magnetic flux caused by said first magnetic interaction and said second magnetic interaction to said object
features.note: The concept of transferring magnetic flux to an object via pole members implies the creation of opposing magnetic poles (north and south) to generate the flux, even if not explicitly stated.
features.refuted: Quote teaches pole members transfer magnetic flux but does not teach first and second pole shoes acting as north and south poles based on magnet position.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: further comprising a tunable actuation system that moves said first arrangement of magnets, said second arrangement of magnets, or both.
features.note: The reference discloses a 'tunable actuation system' for moving the magnets, which could be electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical.
features.refuted: Quote mentions tunable actuation system that moves magnets but does not specify electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical displacement methods.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.quote: further comprising sensors for detecting a distance between said plurality of pole members and said object.
features.note: The reference explicitly discloses sensors for detecting the distance to the object, which can serve as a workpiece sensor.
features.refuted: Quote teaches sensors for detecting distance between pole members and object, not position sensors for gripping/release positions or workpiece sensors.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: While sensors are mentioned, the reference does not describe a specific receptacle in the housing for them or for supply lines.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: wherein said system is integrated in a robotic system.
features.note: Integration into a robotic system implies the presence of an interface for attachment to a manipulator.
features.refuted: Quote only states system is integrated in robotic system, does not teach a manipulator interface for attaching to a manipulator.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not discuss suppressing magnetic field escape or shielding devices.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections or their dimensions relative to workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles in the form of a groove.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles of an active structure on the pole members.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles of an active structure on the pole members.

claims.quote: Provided herein are systems and methods for magnetically gripping an object. A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
claims.note: This passage discloses a magnetic gripping system or gripper for gripping an object, which can be a ferromagnetic workpiece.

claims.quote: moving one or more of said first arrangement of magnets and said second arrangement of magnets to vary their position relative to one another to vary said first magnetic interaction, said second magnetic interaction, or both, to vary said magnetic
claims.note: The reference discloses magnets that are movable to vary magnetic flux, which implies a change in gripping state. However, it does not explicitly state that a single magnet is displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping position and a release position.

claims.quote: a plurality of pole members, wherein said plurality of pole members are (i) in a first magnetic interaction with said first arrangement of magnets and (ii) in a second magnetic interaction with said second arrangement of magnets, wherein each pole
claims.note: This passage discloses pole members that guide magnetic flux to an object, which can be considered a workpiece contact surface.
claims.refuted: The quote mentions pole members in magnetic interaction with magnet arrangements but does not teach attachment to housing, workpiece contact surfaces, or guiding magnetic field portions to contact surfaces.

claims.note: The reference does not disclose a contact surface angle between the workpiece contact surface and the displacement direction, nor does it specify a range for such an angle.
The reference does not disclose a specific contact surface angle for pole members, nor does it mention a range of 170° to 190°.
The reference does not describe a housing extending along a longitudinal axis.
The reference does not describe the displacement direction being aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis of the housing.
The reference mentions pole members transferring magnetic flux but does not describe them having an 'active structure for directing the magnetic field portion'.
This reference does not mention an active structure having a bevel.
This reference does not mention a bevel or a bevel angle.
This reference does not mention a bevel angle or specific ranges for such an angle.

claims.quote: wherein each pole member of said plurality of pole members is configured to transfer magnetic flux caused by said first magnetic interaction and said second magnetic interaction to said object
claims.note: The reference discloses pole members that transfer magnetic flux to an object, which could be considered a form of directing the magnetic field, and it mentions a gripping surface which could be a workpiece contact surface. However, it does not explicitly state that these pole members are 'projections' or that they 'form' the workpiece contact surface.
The reference discusses a plurality of pole members but does not specify them as projections or distinguish between a first and second projection.
The reference does not describe projections being adjacent to one another.
The reference does not describe an active structure with a recess between projections.
The reference does not describe a recess with specific dimensional relationships to projections.
This reference describes a magnetic gripping system but does not explicitly mention a positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece on a workpiece contact surface.

claims.quote: a plurality of pole members, wherein said plurality of pole members are (i) in a first magnetic interaction with said first arrangement of magnets and (ii) in a second magnetic interaction with said second arrangement of magnets
claims.note: The reference teaches a plurality of pole members, which can be interpreted as including at least a first and second pole shoe.
claims.refuted: The quote mentions a plurality of pole members but does not specifically identify or teach a first pole shoe and a second pole shoe.

claims.note: The reference discusses magnetic interactions and varying magnetic flux but does not specify the arrangement of magnets to create distinct north and south poles on specific pole shoes in a gripping position.

claims.quote: a tunable actuation system that moves said first arrangement of magnets, said second arrangement of magnets, or both.
claims.note: The reference teaches that magnets are moved by a tunable actuation system, which implies mechanical or electrical displacement, but does not explicitly mention pneumatic displacement.

claims.quote: The system of claim 1 , further comprising sensors for detecting a distance between said plurality of pole members and said object.
claims.note: The reference discloses sensors for detecting distance to an object, which could be used to infer gripping position, but does not explicitly mention a position sensor for detecting gripping and/or release positions.

claims.quote: The system of claim 1 , further comprising sensors for detecting a distance between said plurality of pole members and said object.
claims.note: The reference discloses sensors for detecting a distance to an object, which could potentially be a workpiece sensor, but it does not explicitly state it detects a 'ferromagnetic workpiece'.
The reference does not disclose a housing having a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor or a supply line.
The reference does not disclose a manipulator interface for attaching the magnetic gripper to a manipulator.
This reference does not mention a housing portion designed to suppress the escape of a magnetic field.
This reference does not mention a shielding device to prevent the magnetic field from escaping the housing.

claims.quote: Provided herein are systems and methods for magnetically gripping an object. A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
claims.note: The abstract describes a magnetic gripping system and a gripper, which aligns with the claim's introduction of a magnetic gripper system.

claims.quote: Provided herein are systems and methods for magnetically gripping an object.
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic gripper for gripping an object, but it does not specifically mention a 'ferromagnetic workpiece' as part of the system itself, only that it grips an 'object'.

claims.quote: A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
claims.note: This passage describes a gripper having tunable gripping states associated with magnetic field strengths, implying that in a gripping state, a magnetic force would press an object.
claims.refuted: The quote mentions tunable gripping states but does not teach a magnet in a gripping position or a ferromagnetic workpiece being pressed against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

claims.quote: A magnetic gripping system may comprise a gripper having different, tunable gripping states that are associated with different magnetic field strengths.
claims.note: This passage describes a gripper having tunable gripping states, which would include a release state where the magnetic force is not applied.
claims.refuted: The quote mentions different gripping states but does not teach a release position where the workpiece is not pressed against contact surfaces.

claims.note: The reference does not discuss specific dimensions of projections or their relationship to the thickness of a ferromagnetic workpiece.
The reference does not describe a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic gripping system with displaceable magnets and pole members for tunable gripping, which aligns well with the core concepts of the subject invention, although specific geometric details are often absent.
